record.paper_title: Non-Supersymmetric (but) Extreme Black Holes, Scalar Hair and Other Open Problems
record.context_brief: Primary versus secondary scalar hair at B-bound saturation
record.original_question: Do there exist supersymmetric supergravity solutions that saturate a generalized Bogomol'nyi bound because of primary scalar charges, or is saturation of the bound always achieved only through secondary scalar hair, where the scalar charge is fixed by conserved electric and magnetic charges rather than being an independent primary charge?

evidence.quote: Scalar charges, not being protected by a gauge symmetry, are not conserved charges. For minimally-coupled scalars the standard no-hair theorems apply and any non-vanishing value implies the presence of naked singularities. The prototype of this kind of singular solution with non-trivial scalar hair (called primary hair) is the one given in Refs. [27] for the theory with a massless scalar ϕ and action

For non-minimally coupled scalars regular BH solutions with secondary scalar hair do exist (just see above). In those solutions, the scalar (dilaton) charge is identical to a certain fixed combinations of the other, conserved, charges

It is not clear whether it should be possible to find supersymmetric solutions which saturate the generalized B bound with primary scalar charges. It seems that, although the B bound should include the primary scalar hair, the saturation of the bound is always reached with secondary scalar hair only, but there is not proof of this fact.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider four-dimensional supergravity theories coupled to scalar fields and Abelian gauge fields, admitting stationary black-hole solutions characterized by an ADM mass M, conserved electric and magnetic charges {q_Λ, p^Λ} (associated with U(1) gauge symmetries), and asymptotic scalar charges Σ_i defined by the 1/r fall-off of the scalar fields φ^i toward their values at spatial infinity. A scalar charge Σ_i is called "secondary" if it is determined by an explicit function Σ_i = Σ_i(q_Λ, p^Λ, φ^i_∞) of the conserved charges and the asymptotic scalar values, and is called "primary" if it is an independent free parameter of the solution not so determined.

Assume the theory admits a generalized Bogomol'nyi (BPS) bound of the form
   M ≥ B(q_Λ, p^Λ, Σ_i, φ^i_∞),
in which primary scalar hair, if present, enters the bound on equal footing with the conserved charges, and assume that saturation M = B characterizes solutions preserving some unbroken supersymmetry.

Question: Does there exist a supersymmetric solution of such a supergravity theory that saturates the generalized Bogomol'nyi bound while carrying at least one primary (independent) scalar charge? Equivalently, must every supersymmetric solution that saturates the generalized bound have all of its scalar charges fixed as secondary hair, i.e. determined by the conserved electric and magnetic charges and the asymptotic scalar values?
artifact.category_tag: Supergravity black holes and BPS bounds
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not locate a definitive proof or counterexample resolving whether supersymmetric supergravity solutions saturating a generalized Bogomol'nyi bound can carry primary scalar hair, or whether saturation always forces the scalar charge to be secondary (a fixed function of the conserved electric/magnetic charges). Standard references on supersymmetric supergravity solutions and attractor mechanisms describe BPS-saturated black holes in which scalar charges are fixed by the conserved charges and asymptotic moduli, but no general theorem ruling out primary-hair BPS saturation was found.

status_evidence.title: Supersymmetric solutions of 4-dimensional supergravities
status_evidence.snippet: In supergravity, supersymmetry imposes the saturation of the BPS bound M = f(q,p,φ_∞), with attractor values of the scalars at the horizon fixed by the conserved charges.
status_evidence.claim: Known supersymmetric BPS-saturated black-hole solutions exhibit secondary scalar hair (scalars determined by conserved charges and asymptotic moduli), but no general theorem excluding primary scalar hair at saturation is asserted.

status_evidence.title: Bogomol'nyi–Prasad–Sommerfield bound - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: BPS states saturate the bound and obey first-order Bogomolny equations.
status_evidence.claim: Generic discussion of BPS saturation does not address the primary vs secondary scalar hair distinction, leaving the specific question without a documented resolution.
